questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Recession speed from the Hubble law
questions.learningObjective: Compute recession speed from Hubble's law
questions.stem: An architect's brief gives a galaxy distance of 100 Mpc and Hubble constant 70 km/s/Mpc, and asks for its recession speed

options.text: 7000 km/s from v equals H0 times d
70 km/s by using distance as 1 Mpc
100 km/s by reading distance as speed
700 km/s by a factor of ten error

questions.explanation: Hubble's law v equals H0 d gives 70 times 100 equals 7000 km/s. Recession speed grows linearly with distance.
questions.hint: Multiply Hubble constant by distance.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Characteristic expansion time from the Hubble constant
questions.learningObjective: Compute the Hubble time from H0
questions.stem: An architect's brief gives H0 as 70 km/s/Mpc, and asks for the characteristic expansion time in billions of years

options.text: About 70 billion years by inverting the wrong quantity
About 14 billion years from 1 over H0
About 1 billion years by a factor of ten error
About 100 billion years by using H0 as 0.7

questions.explanation: Hubble time is 1 over H0, about 14 billion years for H0 70 km/s/Mpc. It sets the timescale of cosmic expansion.
questions.hint: Take the reciprocal of H0 with proper units.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Distance at which the expansion reaches light speed
questions.learningObjective: Compute the Hubble radius
questions.stem: An architect's brief gives H0 as 70 km/s/Mpc, and asks for the distance at which recession speed equals c

options.text: About 43000 Mpc by a factor of ten the other way
About 430 Mpc by a factor of ten error
About 4300 Mpc from c over H0
About 14 Mpc by confusing with Hubble time

questions.explanation: Setting v equals c in Hubble's law gives d equals c over H0, about 4280 Mpc. This is the Hubble radius.
questions.hint: Divide c by H0 with consistent units.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Schwarzschild radius of the Sun
questions.learningObjective: Compute the Schwarzschild radius of the Sun
questions.stem: An architect's brief gives the Sun's mass as 1.99e30 kg, and asks for its Schwarzschild radius in kilometers

options.text: About 2950 km by a factor of 1000 error
About 1.48 km by omitting the factor of 2
options.misconception: omits the factor of 2 in the formula

options.text: About 5.9 km by doubling the correct value
About 2.95 km from 2 G M over c squared

questions.explanation: Schwarzschild radius r_s equals 2 G M over c squared. For the Sun this is about 2.95 km. It is the radius of a black hole of solar mass.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Gravitational clock gain for a navigation satellite
questions.learningObjective: Compute gravitational time dilation for a satellite
questions.stem: An architect's brief asks how much a clock at altitude 20000 km gains per day due to weaker gravity relative to Earth's surface

options.text: About 7 microseconds per day from special relativistic dilation only
About 45 microseconds per day from gravitational dilation
About 0 microseconds because gravity does not affect clocks
About 100 microseconds by a factor of two error

questions.explanation: Clocks higher in a gravitational field run faster. At GPS altitude the gravitational gain is about 45 microseconds per day, larger than the special relativistic loss.

answer.exemplar: The satellite moves at about 3.9 km/s, so special relativity makes its clock run slow by about 7 microseconds per day relative to a clock on Earth's surface.

questions.explanation: Orbital motion causes special relativistic time dilation, making the satellite clock run slow by about 7 microseconds per day. Gravity causes a larger gain.
